clinician.trajectory_summary: A 73-year-old female with history of pelvic radiotherapy for cervical cancer in the 1970s presented to the emergency department with severe haematuria from bilateral nephrostomies and urethra, accompanied by hypotension and tachycardia. She had chronic kidney disease stage 3 and had been managed for several years with bilateral percutaneous nephrostomy tubes and bilateral ureteric stents requiring frequent exchanges for radiotherapy-associated long-segment bilateral distal ureteric strictures. On admission, she was anaemic (Hb 87 g/dL) with normal coagulation studies (INR 1, aPTT 0.75, normal platelets), ruling out coagulopathy as the cause of bleeding. CT angiography revealed the right ureter inseparable from the external iliac artery with an ectatic internal iliac artery. Catheter angiography from the internal iliac artery origin demonstrated active bleeding from the right internal iliac artery into the distal ureter with a linear filling defect consistent with non-occlusive thrombus within the ureter. This confirmed an arteriovenous fistula between the right internal iliac artery and distal right ureter, likely iatrogenic from chronic ureteric stent instrumentation in radiation-damaged tissues. The fistula was successfully managed with interventional radiology assistance.
